title: Build a 3D racing game with no art files using an agent
summary: Jhin Lee had Gemini 4 Argon build a kart racing game in 15 short prompts; he reports about 3.5 hours of build time and zero image or model files.
agent_role: The agent wrote all code, built characters from basic shapes, screenshotted the running game to fix visuals, made music and deployed a web build. The human gave short playtest feedback like 'the music sounds too cheap'.
outcome: Author reports 15 prompts, 3h 26m of active build time, about 12,000 lines of code, and a web version running in under 7 minutes.
what_they_did: Jhin Lee asked Gemini 4 Argon, inside Google's Antigravity tool, for a Mario Kart-style game with no outside art or sound files. He gave casual feedback like a playtester. The agent built characters from simple shapes and screenshotted the game to fix them. It also generated music from instruments built into macOS and published a browser version.
how_it_went: He says it took 15 prompts and about 3.5 hours. The agent spotted a character looked wrong from behind and fixed it. It also traced a broken web deploy to a hidden file blocking graphics.
worth_knowing: It needed pushback: first audio sounded cheap, characters were designed only from the front, and the game started about 22% too fast for humans.
prompt: Build a [type of game] in [framework] using no outside image, model or sound files; generate everything in code. After each change, run the game, take a screenshot, and check it looks right from the player's view. I'll give short playtest feedback and you fix it. When it works, show me how you plan to publish a browser version to [hosting service] and wait for my approval before deploying.

curation.rationale: Detailed walkthrough with live demo and open code, showing the agent checking its own screenshots, generating music and fixing a deploy bug; still a game-building case.
